_meta.purpose: Defines the BOUNDED envelope within which Cadence may personalize a hand-authored plan over time, plus conservative rules for detecting a quality 'deficiency'. The app never authors training or invents sessions; it only nudges emphasis within coach-approved ranges, and only after a real multi-session pattern is observed and confirmed.
_meta.phase: PHASE TWO. Do not build until the core deterministic plan + readiness engine is shipped and real users are generating session logs to test detection against. Detection cannot be validated without real data.

core_design_principles.vetted_floor: Every adjustment stays inside ranges a coach pre-approved per template. The app selects within an envelope; it does not generate.
core_design_principles.asymmetry: REDUCING hard volume is the safe, default, low-evidence response. ADDING hard volume requires more evidence, smaller steps, and gradual ramping. When uncertain, the app reduces or holds — never adds. This matches the anti-overtraining thesis.
core_design_principles.bounded_total: Adjustments are TRADES within a fixed weekly high-CNS budget, not additions on top. To add emphasis in one quality, another is reduced. Total neural load stays capped.
core_design_principles.speed_floor: Maximum-velocity work has a hard weekly minimum that no deficiency response may drop below. The classic 400m mistake is stripping speed to add endurance; this prevents it.
core_design_principles.transparency: No silent plan changes. The app shows the observed pattern in plain language and requires user (and ideally coach) confirmation before altering the plan.
core_design_principles.confounder_exclusion: Sessions flagged low-readiness, or single outlier days, are excluded from deficiency detection so the app doesn't mistake a bad day or under-recovery for a true weakness.

coach_review_checklist: Are the detection thresholds (how much fade, over how many sessions) defensible, or too trigger-happy?
Are the min/max rep bands age-appropriate and is the max a true ceiling?
Is the weekly high-CNS session cap right for the target athlete?
Is the max-velocity weekly floor correct (so speed is never sacrificed)?
Is the 'add' ramp slow enough? (Drafted at <=1 rep/week.)
Should any deficiency response be removed entirely as too risky to automate?

evidence_to_REDUCE.note: Reducing is always safe. Chronic low readiness, repeated incomplete sessions, or a single clearly over-fatigued week can trigger a reduction immediately.

evidence_to_ADD.min_pattern_consistency: pattern present in at least 3 of the last 4 qualifying sessions
exclude_sessions: sessions the user marked as illness/external stress
evidence_to_ADD.ramp: Introduce added volume gradually over 2-3 weeks, re-checking readiness trend each week; abort the add if readiness baseline trends down.
evidence_to_ADD.blackout: Never add hard volume during the Competition/Taper phase, or in any week where the readiness baseline is declining.

never: invent new session types or distances outside the template bands
exceed the weekly high-CNS session cap
drop max-velocity below its weekly floor
add hard volume off a single session or off low-readiness data
change the plan without showing the user the reason

deficiencies.name: late_race_deceleration
deficiencies.plain_language: Times/effort drop noticeably in the final ~20-30m of reps near race distance
detection_signals: measured or RPE-based slowdown in the last third of speed-endurance reps across qualifying sessions

deficiencies.name: weak_top_speed
deficiencies.plain_language: Top-speed (flying) performance lags relative to acceleration ability
detection_signals: max-velocity fly times stagnant while accel is strong, across qualifying sessions

deficiencies.name: chronic_underrecovery
deficiencies.plain_language: Readiness baseline trending down or repeated incomplete high-CNS sessions
detection_signals: repeated failure to complete prescribed reps

reduce.by: drop one high-CNS session to low/tempo, or trim 1-2 reps from the hardest quality

bounded_response.note: Default protective response. Confident and fast.

deficiencies.name: speed_endurance_deficiency
deficiencies.plain_language: Holds top speed only briefly; fades through the second half of 100-150m efforts
detection_signals: progressive slowdown across the back half of speed-endurance/SE1 reps over qualifying sessions

deficiencies.name: weak_top_speed
deficiencies.plain_language: Top speed lags; the 200 is paced rather than sprinted
detection_signals: max-velocity stagnant relative to endurance qualities

deficiencies.name: chronic_underrecovery
deficiencies.plain_language: Readiness baseline trending down or repeated incomplete high-CNS sessions
detection_signals: repeated failure to complete prescribed reps

reduce.by: drop one high-CNS session to tempo, or trim reps from the hardest quality

deficiencies.name: speed_endurance_deficiency
deficiencies.plain_language: The '300m wall' — large fade in the final ~100m; back-half splits decay sharply relative to front half
detection_signals: consistent large positive split / final-segment slowdown in SE1 and SE2 reps over qualifying sessions
self-reported 'dying late' corroborated by logged splits

bounded_response.caution: This is the highest-load adjustment in the whole system. Ramp slowest here; SE2 is the most fatiguing and injury-relevant work. Coach calibration of the split-decay threshold is essential.

deficiencies.name: weak_top_speed
deficiencies.plain_language: Low top-end speed means race pace is too close to max — no speed reserve
detection_signals: max-velocity stagnant or low relative to event level; 100m/200m benchmarks weak vs 400 performance

deficiencies.name: chronic_underrecovery
deficiencies.plain_language: Readiness baseline trending down or repeated incomplete high-CNS sessions (most likely in the demanding Pre-Comp phase)
detection_signals: repeated failure to complete prescribed special-endurance reps

reduce.by: trim SE2 to its minimum and/or convert a high-CNS day to extensive tempo

bounded_response.note: Default protective response, and the most important one for the 400 because Pre-Comp load is heavy. Reduce SE2 first since it carries the highest fatigue cost.
